sentence: HLA-B*15:01 is associated with decreased risk of cutaneous nevirapine hypersensitivity (grade 3–4 rash) when treated with nevirapine in people with HIV-1 infection initiating nevirapine therapy, as compared to non-carriers.
explanation: In a high-resolution HLA case-control study (151 cases, 413 controls) across multiple ethnicities, HLA-B*15:01 clustered with HLA-B*52:01 as protective against cutaneous NVP hypersensitivity.
citations: The most prominent secondary effect is protection associated with the HLA-B B pocket, which is independent of HLA-C risk (OR = 0.18, p = 0.0001 and OR = 0.20, p = 0.0003 for models with and without adjustment for the primary HLA-C cluster) (Fig. 2A).

The B pocket^4, 5^ motif Tyr7-Tyr9-Ala24-Val34-(Met/Thr)45-Glu63-Ile66-Ser67-Asn70-(Tyr/Phe)99 is characteristic of a cluster of HLA-B B62 supertype alleles: HLA-B*15:(01/12/24/25/27/35) and HLA-B*52:01 (Figure S3 and Table S2), consistent with a previously reported protective HLA-B*15 association with cutaneous NVP reactions observed in an Indian population^34^.
Cases (N = 151) and controls (N = 413) were at least 18 years of age, HIV-1-infected, and had previously initiated NVP-containing therapy.
Cases had experienced severe cutaneous toxicity (grade 3 or 4) categorized by National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Disease (NIAID) Division of AIDS criteria.

sentence: HLA-DRB1*04:05 is associated with increased risk (secondary association) of cutaneous nevirapine hypersensitivity when treated with nevirapine in people with HIV-1 infection initiating nevirapine therapy, as compared to non-carriers.
explanation: Logistic regression identified a significant secondary association for DRB1 alleles with a P4 pocket risk motif (including DRB1*04:05) in the case-control cohort.
citations: From MHCcluster (Figure S4) and binding groove analyses of the HLA-DRB1 alleles within the cohort we identified a cluster including both supertype HLA-DR1 and -DR4 alleles (HLA-DRB1*01:(01/02/03) and -DRB1*04:(04/05/08/10), respectively) that exhibited a secondary association with cutaneous NVP HSR (Fig. 2A).
The identified risk alleles for cutaneous NVP HSR share the sequence (Phe/His)13-Gln70-Arg71-Ala74-Tyr78 over residues forming the P4 pocket (Table S4).

sentence: HLA-C*18:01 is associated with increased risk of cutaneous nevirapine hypersensitivity when treated with nevirapine in people with HIV-1 infection of African ancestry, as compared to non-carriers.
explanation: The study identified HLA-C*18:01 as a dominant risk allele in the African subgroup based on shared F pocket features.
citations: In single allele logistic regression analyses HLA-C*04:01 was the only allele for which a consistent, significant predisposing relationship for cutaneous manifestations of NVP HSR was observed across all ancestral groups (Odds ratio (OR) = 3.06 and P = 0.0001 in whole cohort analysis, (Fig. 1A); Asian: OR = 5.49, P = 0.0001; Caucasian: OR = 2.08, P = 0.02; and African: OR = 3.84, P = 0.04).

However, analyses specific to ancestral groups also revealed several other HLA-C allelic associations indicative of HSR predisposition, namely HLA-C*05:01 in Caucasians (versus non-HLA-C*05:01 carriers: OR = 2.84, P = 0.002) and HLA-C*18:01 in patients with African ancestry (versus non-HLA-C*18:01 carriers: OR = 2.67, P = 0.2; vs non-HLA-C*04:01/-C*18:01 carriers: OR = 4.71, P = 0.06).

Moreover, here we demonstrate that the observed association with HLA-C*04 across ethnicities is primarily driven by the unique F pocket motif that HLA-C*04:01 shares with HLA-C*05:01 and HLA-C*18:01 which have dominant effects observed in the Hispanic and African subgroups, respectively.

sentence: HLA-C*04 is associated with increased risk of cutaneous nevirapine hypersensitivity when treated with nevirapine in people with HIV-1 infection initiating nevirapine therapy across multiple ethnicities, as compared to non-carriers.
explanation: The across-ethnicity risk signal for HLA-C*04 was shown to be primarily driven by HLA-C*04:01 in the case-control study.
citations: The HLA alleles most often associated with cutaneous manifestations of NVP HSR are HLA-C*04, commonly carried across ethnicities, as well as HLA-B*35 in Asians and Caucasian patients^19, 21–24^.

In single allele logistic regression analyses HLA-C*04:01 was the only allele for which a consistent, significant predisposing relationship for cutaneous manifestations of NVP HSR was observed across all ancestral groups (Odds ratio (OR) = 3.06 and P = 0.0001 in whole cohort analysis, (Fig. 1A); Asian: OR = 5.49, P = 0.0001; Caucasian: OR = 2.08, P = 0.02; and African: OR = 3.84, P = 0.04).

sentence: HLA-C*04:01 is associated with increased risk of cutaneous nevirapine hypersensitivity when treated with nevirapine in people with HIV-1 infection initiating nevirapine therapy across multiple ethnicities, as compared to non-carriers.
explanation: High-resolution typing and structural modeling identified HLA-C*04:01 as a primary risk allele via an F pocket motif; cohort included 151 cases and 413 controls.
citations: In single allele logistic regression analyses HLA-C*04:01 was the only allele for which a consistent, significant predisposing relationship for cutaneous manifestations of NVP HSR was observed across all ancestral groups (Odds ratio (OR) = 3.06 and P = 0.0001 in whole cohort analysis, (Fig. 1A); Asian: OR = 5.49, P = 0.0001; Caucasian: OR = 2.08, P = 0.02; and African: OR = 3.84, P = 0.04).

We demonstrate that primary predisposition to cutaneous NVP HSR, seen across ancestral groups, can be attributed to a cluster of HLA-C alleles sharing a common binding groove F pocket with HLA-C*04:01.
Four digit HLA typing was available for 151 cases and 413 controls.

sentence: HLA-DRB1*04 (risk subtypes including *04:04, *04:05, *04:08, *04:10) is associated with increased risk (secondary association) of cutaneous nevirapine hypersensitivity when treated with nevirapine in people with HIV-1 infection initiating nevirapine therapy, as compared to non-carriers.
explanation: The DRB1*04 group bearing the P4 pocket risk motif showed a secondary association, while DRB1*04:01 and DRB1*04:15 were protective.
citations: From MHCcluster (Figure S4) and binding groove analyses of the HLA-DRB1 alleles within the cohort we identified a cluster including both supertype HLA-DR1 and -DR4 alleles (HLA-DRB1*01:(01/02/03) and -DRB1*04:(04/05/08/10), respectively) that exhibited a secondary association with cutaneous NVP HSR (Fig. 2A).

In contrast, the predominantly Caucasian alleles HLA-DRB1*04:01 and -DRB1*04:15 differed from the risk group only at position β71 within the P4 pocket, and yet appeared to be protective in this ancestral group (2 cases, 26 controls, p = 0.01).

sentence: HLA-B*57:01 mentioned in article but not studied by paper.
explanation: Cited only as the canonical abacavir hypersensitivity allele; no nevirapine association analysis was performed.
citations: The allelic specificity of the HLA peptide binding groove in the pathogenesis of T cell mediated drug hypersensitivity is exemplified by the well characterized abacavir hypersensitivity syndrome which occurs both in vivo and in vitro only in association with HLA-B*57:01, and not with related B17 serotype alleles such as HLA-B*57:02/3 and HLA-B*58:01.

sentence: HLA-DRB1*04:10 is associated with increased risk (secondary association) of cutaneous nevirapine hypersensitivity when treated with nevirapine in people with HIV-1 infection initiating nevirapine therapy, as compared to non-carriers.
explanation: Identified among DRB1*04 risk alleles via P4 pocket analysis in logistic regression.
citations: From MHCcluster (Figure S4) and binding groove analyses of the HLA-DRB1 alleles within the cohort we identified a cluster including both supertype HLA-DR1 and -DR4 alleles (HLA-DRB1*01:(01/02/03) and -DRB1*04:(04/05/08/10), respectively) that exhibited a secondary association with cutaneous NVP HSR (Fig. 2A).
The identified risk alleles for cutaneous NVP HSR share the sequence (Phe/His)13-Gln70-Arg71-Ala74-Tyr78 over residues forming the P4 pocket (Table S4).
